package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
)

// Every runtime fault recovers as a value that implements error, with the
// runtime's wording; a program's own string panic never does.

var xs = make([]byte, 10)

func report(name string, f func()) {
	defer func() {
		v := recover()
		if v == nil {
			fmt.Println(name, "did not panic")
			return
		}
		err, ok := v.(error)
		if !ok {
			fmt.Printf("%s: not an error: %v\n", name, v)
			return
		}
		fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", name, err.Error())
	}()
	f()
}

type T int

type I interface{ F() }

func (t T) F() {}

// Package-level so the compiler keeps the interface call: the itab wrapper
// is what raises panicwrap's wording, a devirtualised call would fault on
// the dereference instead.
var (
	nilT *T
	nilI I = nilT
)

// A deferred wrapper call binds without fault and panics when it runs, after
// the named result was set.
func deferredWrap() (r int) {
	defer func() { recover() }()
	var i I = nilT
	defer i.F()
	r = 1
	return
}

type M interface{ M() int }

// A method selected on a nil interface inside a return expression raises
// while the callee is being looked up; the frame recovers and returns.
func returnsThroughNil(r M) int { return r.M() }

func recoveredReturn() (out string) {
	defer func() { out = fmt.Sprint("recovered return: ", recover() != nil) }()
	returnsThroughNil(nil)
	return "not reached"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println("deferred wrap:", deferredWrap())
	fmt.Println(recoveredReturn())
	report("index", func() { _ = xs[len(xs)+5] })
	report("nil pointer", func() {
		var p *int
		_ = *p
	})
	report("type assertion", func() {
		var x interface{} = 1
		_ = x.(float32)
	})
	report("divide", func() {
		zero := 0
		_ = 1 / zero
	})
	report("close closed", func() {
		c := make(chan int)
		close(c)
		close(c)
	})
	report("close nil", func() {
		var c chan int
		close(c)
	})
	report("send closed", func() {
		c := make(chan int, 1)
		close(c)
		c <- 1
	})
	report("panicwrap", func() { nilI.F() })
	// Positive control: a value the runtime already boxed as an error.
	report("direct assert", func() {
		defer func() {
			e := recover().(error)
			fmt.Println("direct:", strings.HasPrefix(e.Error(), "runtime error: "))
			panic(e)
		}()
		var m map[string]int
		zero := m["k"]
		_ = 1 / zero
	})
	// Negative: the program's own strings stay strings.
	report("own string", func() { panic("runtime error: not the runtime's") })
	report("own plain", func() { panic("close of nil channel") })
	os.Exit(3)
}
